reviews.result:
**1. High — CLI exclusion silently dropped off the seeded-preset path.** `agent-launch.py:10572-10575` plants the request only into `config["presets"]` dict values, and the sole downstream enforcement (`10683-10691`) fires only when the plan carries `False`. A bare launch (no `--preset`, the pass-through mode named at `10717`) — and any non-dict preset entry skipped by the `isinstance` guard — never receives the seed, so `plan.get(..., True)` stays `True` and the session launches with global instructions included, with no refusal. The gate at `10558` refuses non-private/Codex/resume but not bare, though the spec declares bare invalid. Remedy: refuse the flag at that gate when the launch will not derive its plan from a seeded preset, rather than relying on seeding alone to carry the request.

**2. Medium — NFC rewrite diverges from native matching.** `corpus_session.py:54` normalizes `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/HOME to NFC before emitting `claudeMdExcludes`, but the native loader reads the raw (possibly NFD, common on macOS) value; a byte-level glob mismatch makes exclusion a no-op while pin validation (same NFC recomputation) reports success. Remedy: refuse when `NFC(configured) != configured`, matching the other ambiguity refusals, instead of rewriting.

**3. Medium — cwd inside the config dir defeats exclusion.** The `project != path` guard at `corpus_session.py:68` skips the exact-same-path alias: with cwd under `~/.claude`, the ancestor walk loads `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` as project memory, which User-scope excludes don't remove, so an Exclude launch still includes it. Remedy: refuse when resolved cwd lies inside `path.parent`.

reviews.label: reproduction
reviews.result:
Three material findings, ordered by severity.

**1. High — `--exclude-global-instructions` silently dropped on bare/non-preset launches.** `launch/agent-launch.py:10572-10575` seeds only `config["presets"]` dict entries. A plan not built from a seeded preset entry (bare no-preset launch; Vanilla too, if it is synthesized rather than stored in `presets`) defaults `include_global_instructions` to True, so the guard chain at `10683` never fires: no refusal, and the session launches with global instructions included despite the explicit flag. The spec declares bare invalid for this flag, meaning refusal, not silence — golden "Exclude launches included." Remedy: in the `10558` block, refuse when the launch will not consume a seeded preset, or set the choice on the resulting plan and let the existing guards fire.

**2. Medium — resume silently discards an explicit exclusion request.** `compose/corpus_session.py:667-668`: `_global_instruction_choice` runs only `if not resume_id`, so `launch(..., resume_id=X, include_global_instructions=False)` on an include-recorded pin validates nothing and replays the include argv — silent inclusion instead of refusal. Only the CLI layer (`10585-10594`) guards this; every other module entry re-raises itself. Remedy: raise `SessionError` in `launch` when `resume_id` is set and `include_global_instructions` is False.

**3. Low — pin-time revalidation can terminate a healthy session.** `corpus_session.py:520` recomputes exclusion patterns inside `observe_and_pin` using `restore_environment(record, {})` plus live symlink/alias checks; any drift (e.g., a symlink appearing under `rules/`, or provenance not reproducing the launch env) raises inside the polling loop (`700-710`), whose `finally` kills the running child (`712-717`) instead of the designed retained-for-recovery exit. Remedy: catch `SessionError` there, warn, and let the child continue.

reviews.label: security
reviews.result:
Two material findings; no path was found where the added `--settings` clobbers user settings (compose_argv at corpus_session.py:364 refuses any pre-existing `--settings`, matching the spec).

**1. High — agent-launch.py:10558–10575 (flag seeding) plus guard at :10683.** `--exclude-global-instructions` acts solely by setting `include_global_instructions=False` on dicts in `config["presets"]`, and every downstream refusal fires only when the plan carries False. A launch whose plan is not built from those dicts — the bare/no-preset pass-through mode the code itself documents at :10716, or any preset synthesized outside `config["presets"]` — defaults to True, so the :10683 guard never triggers and the session launches with global instructions included despite the explicit exclusion flag. The spec says bare is invalid; resume (:10585) and non-private (:10559) are refused, bare is not. Remedy: refuse the flag in that same guard cluster whenever no config-preset-backed plan will be built, mirroring the resume check.

**2. Medium — corpus_session.py:515–533 `observe_and_pin`, called from the launch polling loop (:700–717).** For an exclude session, every pin attempt re-runs `_record_instruction_choice` (:520), which re-walks the rules tree for symlinks (:59–63). If a symlink appears under `~/.claude/rules` between launch and host evidence (dotfile managers do this), the SessionError is uncaught — the loop has no `except` before `finally` (:711) — so the finally block terminates the user's healthy running session rather than retaining the activation as the :707–708 path does. Remedy: catch SessionError around the pin attempt, warn and retain the activation, and leave the child running.

reviews.label: final
reviews.result:
**One concrete failure path; otherwise scoped clean.**

**Silent inclusion via `..` through a symlink in CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.** `_claude_global_instruction_patterns` (corpus_session.py:54) collapses the configured value lexically with `os.path.normpath` before building patterns and before the symlink walk at line 61. Input: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/Users/x/link/../.claude`, where `/Users/x/link → /opt/target`. The adapter excludes `/Users/x/.claude/CLAUDE.md` plus `rules/**`, and the guard walks only the collapsed path's components, so the symlink is never seen. Native Claude applies no path normalization to the env value (only NFC), and the kernel resolves `link/..` to `/opt`, so it loads `/opt/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `/opt/.claude/rules/**`, which neither the literal patterns nor their resolved variants match. The launch proceeds claiming exclusion while global instructions load. Cheap fail-closed fix: refuse when `normpath(configured) != configured`, mirroring the metacharacter guard.

Otherwise clean within scope: existing `--settings` is refused, never dropped (lines 370–374), and `_record_instruction_choice` enforces exactly one matching value against the same environment the native process receives, fresh and resume; Codex, Vanilla, and bare-launch refusals are present; nothing writes to or deletes from the native home; observe-loop exclusion checks use `check_paths=False`, so later filesystem changes cannot terminate a running session.

Review an implemented, bounded feature: agent-bios active sessions default to including existing user-global instruction files, with explicit exclusion. No source/global files should be rewritten. Project instruction files and project memory, authentication, tool registration, and execution permissions should remain native. The one new preset/plan/journal field is include_global_instructions (bool, default true; old pins missing it mean true). CLI --exclude-global-instructions seeds an invocation-local config copy before Custom/save; the final visible Custom choice wins. It is not valid for Vanilla/bare/non-private or with resume overrides. Managed resume reuses its recorded choice.

Current supported exclusion: Claude >=2.1.263, through one --settings JSON with claudeMdExcludes of exact global CLAUDE.md plus global rules/**. Native loader excludes these User sources before parsing. Native arrays union/dedup across configuration layers. --settings repetition is last-wins, so an existing --settings argument is explicitly refused; it must not be replaced. Relative/empty config dirs, symlinks/glob metacharacters, and project/global aliases are refused because exclusion would be ambiguous. Managed/policy instructions and independent tool/skill registrations are outside this option.

Codex 0.153.4 has no native selective-global route. A macOS OS-deny prototype removed global input but broke actual `codex sandbox -- /usr/bin/true` (baseline exit 0, wrapper exit 71); no such wrapper is implemented. Codex exclusion is disabled/refused, never silently treated as inclusion. This unsupported platform is a disclosed boundary, not a claim that the full cross-host request is complete.

Criterion: behavioral/false-signal review. Report only concrete input -> branch -> wrong behavior in the supplied new implementation. Give severity, source/function anchor, and minimal remedy. No speculative missing tests, style suggestions, unrelated old feature findings, or redesign outside the declared support. Goldens: + an Exclude selection launches with global sources included; + --settings silently drops user permissions; - a correctly refused unsupported Codex setting; - different rule wording with identical operation; boundary: reading native configuration instructions is intentionally retained (this option concerns global instruction documents/rules, not all configuration or skill metadata).

Real evidence: actual managed corpus_session.launch include/exclude startup on Claude 2.1.263 showed 7 versus 3 memory sources. Global CLAUDE.md, its two imports, and user rules disappeared; project CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and project memory remained. Native login banner and permission mode remained; four protected instruction/settings files had equal before/after hashes. No model prompt/generation was requested. Runtime/unit suite and real Codex loader tests pass; UI picker and default projection tests pass. These are evidence, not a substitute for your own source check.

Read only this self-contained packet (source excerpts follow). Do not call tools or spawn reviewers. Return at most three material findings or a concise scoped no-findings statement, <=250 words. This is a fresh independent implementation review; the target is the supplied revision.
